1ror1xf: When she returned to the station, Elena had not seen her brother for twenty years. She had traveled all night and expected to recognize him by the way he walked, because recent photographs seemed strange to her. On the platform there was a man with a blue suitcase, but it was not him. Elena looked at the clock and remembered the last argument, the one in which they had both promised never to ask each other for anything again. They had written to each other afterwards, brief messages that carefully avoided the reason for the parting.
kmncfj: Then the cell phone rings. «Did you arrive yet? Come to the side exit; I'm waiting for you in the car.» His voice had not changed as much as she had feared. Elena froze for a few seconds before answering. At another time she would have corrected the expression salida del costado, as if the way of naming a door could say something about the way of living. Now she simply asked which side she should go to. The building had been renovated and she did not want to turn a practical doubt into another small battle.
1wilas8: Her brother was standing next to an old car. «You have the same suitcase,» he said, and smiled without coming closer yet. Elena was about to answer no, that she had bought that one recently, when she saw a mark on the handle. The suitcase was not hers. During the trip she had picked up an identical one and had not noticed until that moment. They looked at each other and began to laugh, first with surprise and then with an ease neither had foreseen.
1wqhbly: They had to go back to the counter, explain the mistake, and wait for news of the right luggage. They did not talk then about the lost years. They talked about labels, phones, and schedules, and that ordinary conversation allowed them to stay together without demanding an immediate reconciliation. Elena had imagined a meeting capable of resolving everything. In the end, a wrong suitcase offered them something more modest: a shared matter they did know how to start talking about.
